newsitem.title: UK: Crude oil tanker rates - Mideast/east routes flat.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil tanker rates - Mideast/east routes flat.

text.p: Rates for very large crude carriers (VLCCs) for eastwards routes from the Middle East were flat on Tuesday despite a flurry of fixtures, while rates for 80,000 tonne Aframaxes in the Med were up, shipping brokers said.

At least nine VLCCs and two ULCCS (ultra large crude carriers) were seen fixed from Middle Eastern ports to destinations eastwards from India, while two VLCC fixtures were seen fixed at around W58 on Mideast/South Africa routes.
Mideast/Japan VLCCs were little changed at around W67.5, with plenty of tonnage available to cater for good demand.
Rates in the Caribbbean for 75,000 tonners were firmer as a shortage of vessels bit. One broker assessed the market there for ships of this size at a sturdy W120.
"There are not so many ships around as they are on the continent at the moment," he said.
Rates for UK/Cont for Aframaxes were heard languishing around W95, with DEA seen fixing one vessel at this level and Shell fixing another at W97.5.
West African chartering for million-barrel Suezmaxes was quieter and dealers saw rates at or above W100.
Cross-Med rates were boosted by good demand for Aframaxes and brokers said bad weather had added another layer of support.
Modern Aframaxes were fixed at W105 and W107.5. Older ships, however, still commanded sharply lower rates and dealers said they had moved only a little above last week's W97.5 fixtures.

"We had some quiet days recently where rates went down, but now with new enquiries we see these coming up to normal levels again," one dealer said. "It is a two-tier market." Dealers said bad weather in the Mediterranean was continuing to keep the Italian ports of Fiumicino and Falconara closed. Problems at Skikda had been solved, they added, but had no details.
